exposure: previous term (≥37 weeks' gestation), full-dilatation cesarean delivery
scar position relative to the internal cervical os
outcome: need for prophylactic interventions (vaginal cervical cerclage or vaginal progesterone)
cohort: Singleton pregnant women (14 to 24 weeks' gestation) with a previous term full-dilatation cesarean delivery who attended a high-risk preterm birth surveillance clinic
finding: Cesarean delivery scar characteristics, particularly a scar located <5.0 mm above or below the internal cervical os, were associated with an increased risk of spontaneous preterm birth and short cervical length in women with a previous full-dilatation cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: A low cesarean delivery scar can compromise the functional integrity of the internal cervical os, leading to cervical shortening and/or spontaneous preterm birth.
